description:
We are The Astro Voyagers from Daffodil International University, Bangladesh: Md Abdul Quym Shanto (Lead), Sajid Ahasan (AI/ML), Tawhid Ahmed Saad (Backend), MD Sabbir Hossien (Frontend & UI), Arpita Kundu (Data & Research) and Mahabub Hasan (Media). We built FarmShield AI: seven NASA datasets help farmers compare crop rotations and see flood, water and crop-health risks for their field, in Bangla or English.

Try it: https://farm-shield-ai-pi.vercel.app
summary: FarmShield AI helps farmers in Bangladesh, and anywhere in the world, plan next season's crops and see today's risks for their own field. In Bangladesh nearly half of all workers live from farming, and one flood or one drought can take a whole season. In the rotation planner, a farmer says what they grow, what matters most and what their soil is like; FarmShield compares that rotation with three others and shows its reasons, the NASA evidence, and what is still unknown. NASA GRACE groundwater lowers the score of thirsty crops where groundwater keeps running low, as in Barind, and on haor land the plan uses only the dry months. Any field gets three ratings (flood risk, water stress and crop health), each with its reason and NASA source. It uses SMAP soil moisture, GPM IMERG rainfall, MODIS and VIIRS vegetation, NASA POWER climate, SRTM elevation, GRACE groundwater and GIBS imagery. Farmers can ask by voice or text in Bangla or English, and get short Bangla SMS warnings on basic phones. FarmShield supports a farmer's judgment; it never replaces it.
details:
Live app: https://farm-shield-ai-pi.vercel.app

240-second video: https://youtu.be/2l9c27RkGoQ

Code: https://github.com/aqshanto/FarmShield-AI

THE CHALLENGE

Field Shift asks for a tool that helps farmers explore crop-rotation strategies with NASA data: compare at least three options, including the current one, explain why, and support (not replace) the farmer's judgment. In Bangladesh nearly half of all workers live from farming, and one flood or one drought can take a whole season.

WHAT WE BUILT

FarmShield AI is a free web app (phone-friendly, English and Bangla) with five parts:

1. Rotation planner: the farmer says what they grow, what matters most and what their soil is like. FarmShield compares that rotation with three others and shows, for each, the reasons, the NASA evidence, the benefits, the risks and what we don't know yet. Example: in Barind a field sits bare for four months; Mustard, Mungbean and Aman cuts that to two, and mungbean feeds the soil. On haor land, under water half the year, it plans only for the dry months.

2. Field ratings: any farmer can add their own field anywhere in the world and get three clear ratings (flood risk, water stress, crop health), each with its reason, its NASA source and what to do.

3. Risk map of all of Bangladesh and the world, on NASA GIBS imagery.

4. Farmer assistant: ask about your field by voice or text, in Bangla or English; answers can be read aloud.

5. SMS preview: when something needs action, a short Bangla warning for basic phones.

HOW IT WORKS (NASA DATA AT THE CORE)

- SMAP (SPL3SMP_E): how wet the soil is, for water stress.

- GPM IMERG (GPM_3IMERGDL): daily rain, for flood risk and water stress.

- MODIS (MOD13Q1, MYD13Q1): how green the crops are (NDVI), for crop health.

- VIIRS (VNP13A1, VJ113A1): the long-term greenness baseline, what normal looks like for each place.

- NASA POWER: each place's usual climate (monthly rain, temperature), the evidence in the rotation planner.

- SRTM: height of the land, because low land floods first.

- GRACE / GRACE-FO (GRACEDADM_CLSM025GL_7D): groundwater at the end of each dry season. In Barind it was low in three of the first ten years and seven of the last ten, so thirsty crops score lower there.

- GIBS: the satellite map layers.

The ratings and rotation scores are fixed, explainable rules over this data (no black box). Every answer shows where it came from and what is still unknown.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Smallholder farmers first, especially on basic phones and with little reading in English; also agriculture officers and NGOs who advise many farmers. A farmer can see, before planting, which rotation suits their field and the climate it is heading into, and act early on a flood or a dry spell.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

It turns seven NASA datasets into plain words, icons and colours a farmer understands, in their own language, by voice or text. It shows what it doesn't know as clearly as what it does. It works for any field on Earth, not only Bangladesh.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Low literacy and basic phones (voice, read-aloud, icons, SMS); trust (every judgment shows its NASA source and its limits; the farmer decides); local farming (Barind's falling groundwater, haor land under water half the year); slow internet (a warm cache and a demo mode).

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Framer Motion, MapLibre GL, Lucide icons, Noto Sans Bengali. Backend: Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, httpx, pytest. Hosting: Vercel (website) and Render (API). AI: Claude by Anthropic (assistant wording, help with code, logo), described in full in docs/AI_USE.md. Open source under the MIT license.

WHAT'S NEXT

Test FarmShield with farmers and Upazila agriculture officers, check its ratings against past floods and droughts, send real SMS alerts, and add more crops and regions.

USE OF AI

Claude by Anthropic: the wording of the app's farmer assistant, help writing code, and the logo (full disclosure: docs/AI_USE.md). ChatGPT by OpenAI: the group photo on our team page was made by ChatGPT from our six real individual photos, which we asked it to combine into one team photo; we did not save the exact prompt. All other work (NASA data analysis, ratings, video script, narration, screen recordings) is our own.
